title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the power layer of a data center build, not a failure of a model or of software. Sixty-two natural gas generators were installed and operated at the Vineland construction site without the permits the state requires for either. The campus was already partly in use, so the unpermitted equipment was not idle stock waiting on approval.

Catching it would have taken a permit check before installation and a second one before operation, at the point where generators are procured and commissioned. The state's inspectors found the generators in late July, after they were in place, and the fine followed. The county health department's noise orders and the homeowners' federal suit describe the same pattern, with oversight arriving after equipment is already running.

What is not established is intent, since the reporting does not say the operator set out to skip permitting, and the homeowners' federal lawsuit is a complaint rather than a finding.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million on Tuesday after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center construction site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. The fine was for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act and is the largest ever issued to a New Jersey data center operator, state officials said.

The Vineland campus is slated for completion at the end of the year. It will be 2.6 million square feet and need 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium size city. Some of it is already in use. The project has drawn complaints, including a federal lawsuit by homeowners over persistent noise and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said at a Climate Week event that data center builders must not be exempt and that development must benefit New Jersey communities.
